answer: Ripple-tracing correlation audit. Each agent action emits a low-amplitude whisper of timing and resource-usage metadata; a post-hoc detector clusters identities whose noise signatures correlate above threshold across independent tasks. Flagged clusters face retroactive settlement: the operator pays a penalty proportional to cluster size, plus forfeiture of all rewards earned. A willow of corroborating traces must accumulate before action, so attackers pay full operational cost per identity while detection cost stays flat.
